questions.q: What are the four parts of a PL/SQL block, in order?
options: DECLARE, BEGIN, EXCEPTION, END
BEGIN, DECLARE, END, EXCEPTION
TRY, CATCH, BEGIN, END
DECLARE, EXCEPTION, BEGIN, END
questions.explain: Every PL/SQL block follows this same order: optional DECLARE, required BEGIN...END, optional EXCEPTION before the final END.

questions.q: Which part of a PL/SQL block can never be omitted?
options: BEGIN...END
DECLARE
EXCEPTION
All three parts are optional
questions.explain: DECLARE and EXCEPTION are both optional. BEGIN...END, the executable section, is the only part that is always required.

questions.q: A variable declared inside a nested inner block's DECLARE section is visible:
options: Only for the life of that inner block
For the rest of the entire outer block
For the entire session, like an Oracle package variable
Nowhere — nested blocks cannot declare variables
questions.explain: Nested blocks give each inner block its own scope — once the inner block's END runs, its locally declared variables are gone.

questions.q: Why doesn't T-SQL's BEGIN...END give the same scoping behavior as a PL/SQL block?
options: T-SQL's BEGIN...END only groups statements; a DECLARE inside it is still scoped to the whole batch or procedure, not to that BEGIN...END
T-SQL doesn't have a BEGIN...END keyword pair at all
T-SQL's BEGIN...END always throws an error if a variable is declared inside it
T-SQL's BEGIN...END behaves identically to a PL/SQL block in every way
questions.explain: T-SQL BEGIN...END is purely a statement-grouping construct used in IF, WHILE, and procedures — it carries no variable scope of its own, unlike a PL/SQL block.

questions.q: In a named PL/SQL procedure, what plays the same role as a DECLARE section in an anonymous block?
options: The IS (or AS) section between the procedure header and BEGIN
The parameter list in parentheses
A separate CREATE DECLARE statement
There is no equivalent — named procedures cannot have local variables
questions.explain: A named procedure's body is the same block structure with a name and parameter list attached; IS/AS introduces the same kind of section DECLARE does in an anonymous block.
